messages:
morgan: Heads up — publish pipeline failed on the samplekit release job. typegen bumped the client semver unexpectedly and npm publish was blocked. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
ci-bot: publish-job-7423 failed: exit code 1. Error: changelog.semver_check failed. Detected version diff: 1.2.3 -> 1.3.0 (expected patch). See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/7423
elaine: looking. I saw a weird auth/retry unit test flake on the sample app earlier this morning. Not sure if it's related but the sample app uses the local built SDK to run regen tests which can change type-hash ordering.
josh: @elaine that ordering drift can trigger typegen to reclassify some breaking/non-breaking changes because of property reordering in the OpenAPI -> types step. Did TypeGen run with the new op spec?
elaine: yep, typegen ran after the sample app onboarding CI job re-ran against the staging spec. The spec had a small property reorder from a recent backend change (non-breaking logically). Our stable-sort hasn't kicked in for the generator run for that commit.
pat: summary: CI flow = build SDK -> sample app integration tests -> run typegen/regenerate -> run changelog/semver check -> publish. If sample app uses the built SDK, a flake in auth/retry tests can force a rebuild with slightly different serialization ordering, causing a regen diff and a semver bump.
morgan: ugh. Two questions: (1) can we stop the sample app from using the artifact that triggers regen during the publish gating job, and (2) is there a safe way to auto-normalize property ordering so typegen doesn't flip minor/patch?
josh: for (1) we can change the publish pipeline to use the last tagged SDK for the integration tests rather than the freshly built one during the publish job. That would avoid bootstrap churn. For (2) adding a stable sort pass in typegen before diffing fixes a lot of noise — I proposed this in the typegen backlog a while ago.
elaine: i've got a quick patch that enforces deterministic ordering across properties and enums; it needs a unit test and a semver-run in CI. I can open a PR. It should prevent these spurious minor bumps.
ci-bot: Note: failing job artifacts preserved at s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/publish/7423. Changelog diff: `- 1.2.3 -> 1.3.0` generated by typegen-ctl v0.18.2
pat: short-term mitigation: allow a manual override label `publish/allow-doc-only` that a releaser can apply for changes that only affect generator ordering. Longer term: the stable-sort + sampleapp fix.
morgan: agree. Can you @josh and @elaine coordinate a tiny pipeline patch + typegen PR? I'd like a quick rollback path if this happens during a Friday release. Also add a one-line doc in the release guide about the override label and who can approve.
josh: will do. I'll open the pipeline PR to pin sampleapp test artifact to latest tag. ETA EOD.
elaine: opening typegen PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/typegen/pull/459 — adds stable property sort + unit tests. cc @pat
pat: i'll add the `publish/allow-doc-only` label to repo settings and update release checklist. Also adding a CI flake hook to warn if auth/retry tests fail during the publish flow so we don't accidentally regenerate.
morgan: awesome. One more ask — can we add a small automatic check in the semver guard that says "if the diff is only ordering/whitespace in generated types, treat as docs-only"? Means adding a normalized comparison step, but would save headaches.
elaine: that's the plan for PR #459, it emits a normalized diff indicator. If it surfaces as only ordering changes, the semver guard will flag as docs-only. I'll add tests for the builder.
josh: tagging @releases for visibility. Also adding a short blurb in the devex-runbook about not running typegen after sampleapp integration in the publish job until this is patched.
morgan: thanks everyone. If we can get the two PRs merged tomorrow morning we should be safe for the weekend release. :thumbsup:
